title: The syllabus GEMM, in C
hints: Start from the plain triple loop: `C[i][j]` is the sum over `k` of `A[i][k] * B[k][j]`.
Only the A access changes. A is stored transposed, so `A[i][k]` lives at `At[k*M + i]`. B is ordinary: `B[k*N + j]`.
C starts full of junk. Sum into a local accumulator that starts at 0, then store it into `C[i*N + j]`, instead of adding to whatever C already holds.
explain: The reference is the standard i, j, k loop with A read as `At[k*M + i]`. It sums into a local `acc = 0` and writes `C[i*N + j] = acc`, so the 99s already in C never leak into the result.
